title.narrative: ASFC Främja mänskliga rättigheter och kamp mot straffrihet i Guatemala 2024-2026
ASFC Strengthening human rights and fighting impunity in Guatemala 2024-2026

description.narrative: Lawyers Without Borders (LWBC eller Abogados Sin Fronteras, ASFC, på spanska) är en icke­statlig organisation för internationellt utvecklingssamarbete med säte i Quebec i Kanada och med syfte att stödja försvaret av mänskliga rättigheter för människor i utsatta situationer genom att stärka tillgången till rättvisa och juridisk representation. ASFC:s arbete i Guatemala är mycket relevant för Sveriges strategi 2021-­2025 och väl i linje med strategins första mål: "Stärkta förutsättningar för demokrati och ökad respekt för mänskliga rättigheter och rättsstatens principer."

Lawyers Without Borders (LWBC or Abogados Sin Fronteras, ASFC, in Spanish) is a non-governmental organization for international development cooperation based in Quebec, Canada, with the aim of supporting the defense of human rights for people in vulnerable situations by strengthening access to justice and legal representation. ASFC's work in Guatemala is very relevant to Sweden's strategy 2021-2025 and well in line with the strategy's first goal: "Improved conditions for democracy and increased respect for human rights and the rule of law."

Sida supports ASFC's strategic plan and operations in Guatemala as a whole, enabling ASFC to contribute to the fulfillment of the human rights of people in vulnerable situations and strengthening access to justice and legal representation.
In 2024-2025, ASFC will offer legal support to human rights defenders facing attacks or unfounded persecution for their work on high-profile legal cases regarding anti-corruption, grave human rights violations, and similar.
ASFC will also assist civil society organizations working on transitional justice regarding grave human rights violations, supporting Guatemala's ongoing transition to democracy.
Additionally, ASFC will also provide legal services to women, girls and boys who have survived human trafficking and sexual violence, and strengthen capacities among actors working to prevent such crimes.
